content.label: This is the Great app

I’ve tried almost all of the health/activity apps, and I have kept 3. Gentler Streak is the best one for health/activity combined for me. They are constantly updating the app with new features and refining its current functions. I was very active a few years ago but got myself in a slump, and now I’m digging myself out. Gentler Streak has been helping me do that, watching my health/activity levels. I can’t wait to see what they do next! Oh and I forgot to mention, their support is amazing!
You cannot really try this app without purchasing premium. No real features in free means I have no idea what the app is about or whether it can help me.

title.label: I love this app! Two wishes…

content.label:
As a long-time endurance athlete, it’s easy to get sucked into comparison. My friend did this, I’m falling behind. Oh, my run today was really slow, I need to make an excuse in my Strava workout description so people have context and don’t think poorly of me. It’s more exhausting than the actual long runs. 

Gentler is the perfect antidote. Instead of obsessing over what other people are doing or the optics of what I’m doing, I can focus on what my body needs. Novel idea in the age of social media! Plus it still has the data I need to train effectively, unlike many “alternative” exercise tracking apps. 

Also love that the nutrition and exercise tips are rooted in science, not diet culture. Whole posts about how beneficial carbs and fat are? Major green flag 💚

I only have two complaints, and these are missing features/opportunities rather than broken current ones. 

1. I wish there was better integration for folks not using an Apple Watch. I have a very nice GPS watch with the battery life needed for running ultras, so no intention of ever switching to an Apple Watch.

Unfortunately, I run into barriers with this app, like not being able to use or even view the suggested Gentler workouts. I wish there was a way to export them to Coros, or even just look at their details in the app so I can manually program a workout on my watch (or at least know what to shoot for).

2. I wish I could edit activities, especially activity types, within the Gentler app. Once an activity is exported from my watch to the app, I can’t edit the type. 

So for example, since my watch doesn’t have a specific yoga mode and I use the “gym cardio” mode, Gentler views my yoga activities as weightlifting (or other), and I can’t change it. Same goes for trail running, mountain biking, etc. Gentler offers those as supported activities types but I wish I could change my already imported workouts to those supported types like is possible in Strava.

It’s not the end of the world, but when viewing monthly and yearly data, I’d love to be able to differentiate between days I actually lifted weights and when I did yoga, or how many times I rode my mountain bike versus road bike.

At the end of the day, pretty minor things that won’t keep me from using the app, but I think it would take the overall user experience to a new level!

Thank you for making an app for recovering comparison addicts like myself. It’s really helpful for reframing my fitness journey and helping me focus on the activity and how it benefits my body instead of how it looks to others.

Difficult to navigate with many screens that are full of text.
Plus, this app doesn’t show steps at all. (Only miles)

title.label: Apple Watch 8 with the latest WatchOS issue

content.label: App stuck on “discarding workout” forever. Reboots don't help. Must reinstall app every time, very annoying
This app is really helping me pace myself. I often get started and then get in a slump. Not with this app.

So the idea behind the app is supposed to support you in a more relaxed kind of way. Meanwhile I’m doing a workout struggling to finish and it will say “congratulations! Doing this will maintain your fitness” or even better “to improve Do a more intense workout” meanwhile I’m exhausted and sweating.  I’m doing my best don’t patronize me 🫠

The app in question was a textbook example of a subpar user experience. Its interface was cluttered and confusing, making it a challenge to navigate and find the desired features. The app frequently crashed, leaving users frustrated and often unable to complete even the most basic tasks. To add to the frustration, it bombarded users with intrusive and irrelevant ads, disrupting the overall usability. Furthermore, customer support was virtually non-existent, making it nearly impossible to address any issues or seek assistance. In sum, the app's poor design, constant crashes, and lack of support made it an infuriating and overall unpleasant experience for users.

title.label: Loved until the watch app stopped working

content.label:
Update: 
My watch just aged out of the app. If you have a newer Apple Watch, it should work great for you. Huge bummer that my otherwise perfectly functional device will no longer support this app that I used all day everyday but I guess maybe I can get back into regular use when I am able to afford a new watch 🤷🏻‍♀️. Better than the Apple fitness rings if it works on your Watch. 

Original review:
I started paying for this app earlier this year and absolutely loved it for the first half of 2023. After an update about a month ago, maybe longer, the watch app totally stopped working then disappeared from my watch. I have tried redownloading to my watch periodically since incase it is fixed by a subsequent update and every time I am told the download failed and to try again later. Anyone else having this problem? I really loved the app so I hope it is resolved quickly.

title.label: After a full week of resting I’m still “overreaching”

content.label:
I don’t know what the intent behind this app is, because all it seems to say is that I’m overreaching. I took two short (10 min ea) bike rides and it said I was overreaching for a day before telling me to exercise. Then I took one long bike ride (2 hrs) a week ago and today it still says I’m overreaching and need to rest. I haven’t even taken walks since then! If you want to build your fitness level go find an app that will actually push you. If you want to feel good about being lazy download this app. 

 Edit: I just got a message that I need to log a workout (even though I just did one yesterday) and it STILL says I’m overreaching.

Edit 2: I didn’t open it for a couple weeks and the widget said for all of that time that I was either well rested or overreaching. It never said I was on the right track and it took days to go from overreaching to the well rested, never stopping in the middle. Then today I got a mea culpa message when I opened the app saying their onboarding was messed up and they were going to fix that. Near as I can tell nothing has been fixed. Go find another app, this one is not good.

Generally a good app, good advice and creates a useful record, but one BIG problem.  The problem is that sometimes I inadvertently hit a button on my watch and the app records a workout that becomes a permanent part of my record though nothing really happened.  I need the ability to edit and tweak the records created to make sure they properly reflect what I actually did.  Without that, the records are faulty and not nearly so useful as the app would like to make me think they are.

You’re doing great! Keep it up! 

That’s all great but give me some data. I want to know when I should push harder and how hard compared to yesterday or ??  Give me something. Other apps use all of the health data that Gentler does but other apps give you a “where is your recovery” today and a goal range. It doesn’t say walk x miles but lets you know to take it easy today or if I’m near 100% and push hard. Every day I have a long workout or game, Gentler gives me a “hold up buddy. Know your limits”. 

I guess this is ok for most people (based on reviews) but I want a little more than a pat on the back and a “keep it up!”

Interface is nice for what it is. Cheers

I adore this app. Although I wish it had more features, I love how it simplifies everything. I used to be heavily into bodybuilding, and lifting heavy. I still train hard, although considerably lighter. I don’t want or need granular metrics. The high-level overview is enough. Plus, the app has a cheerful, cute presentation, which makes it a joy to use. The stickers were a nice touch.

This app is so underrated. My wife and I started using this app to track our progress and we love it. It stays true to its name: A gentler way to track your fitness and overall health. There’s something beautiful in its simplicity without overwhelming the user. It’s the Goldilocks of fitness app in my opinion. 

This is coming from a former US Marine & current SWAT team member. 

Thanks for your hard work on this app. I wish you all the best and hope for long lasting success for your app.
I love it!
The instructions say to swipe left to see a fitness path, but I can’t figure out how to make that happen.
Leverage Apple Watch ability to detect walking or running! It would also be useful to be able to track Gym activities

The graphic 'you seem well rested' is really inappropriate for when I've just gotten done telling the app I've been sick all week. Though, more importantly, it doesn't take that into consideration on how I should be able to be active or not. 
  And on a more personal note, saying 'the pandemic is long since over' is extremely insensitive to those of us who will probably have to mask for the rest of our lives.

title.label: Ridiculous and discouraging feedback from app

content.label:
I’ve used the app over two months and found if anything it has a negative impact on my physical health and the statements about my health just piss me off. I spent a week on vacation walking and hiking in the mountains. Even on light days that I considered no exertion the app screamed at me that I was overdoing it. After returning home and not exercising for 2 days it was still threatening that dire things would happen if I didn’t rest. Then I wake this morning to it flipping 180 over night and now telling me my fitness is in decline from not exercising! Sadly, inaccurate, alarming, and wildly extreme comments like this are normal for this app. 
The flip flopping and inaccuracy of the comments makes this worthless. Wish I hadn’t spent money on it but the free/trial version was too pared down to know what it does. Going back to just using apple fitness, it actually reflects what I do in a day whether I start it tracking or not.

title.label: One of the best fitness apps out there

content.label: I think this is probably the best fitness app I’ve tried, and I’ve definitely been able to lose weight and have a consistent workout routine. The only thing that’s keeping me from giving it 5 stars is that I really wish it had some strength training workouts that I could follow. Otherwise I think it’s a great app and a creative approach to working out!

title.label: The right way to be (re)introduced to fitness

content.label:
Gentler Streaks makes fitness accessible to all. It lowers the barrier to entry (your own mind!) and does so in a fun and delightful way. As someone who has always had a complicated relationship with fitness and who has tried lots of apps to track workouts or provide motivation, this one is by far the best.

Gentler Streaks combines the tracking necessities with the appropriate motivation to help you continually achieve your fitness goals. No matter if you’re a novice runner or an expert powerlifter, there’s something in this app for you. It’ll tell you when it’s time to give your body a break and when it’s time to push to the next level.

The added benefit of Wellbeing, which utilizes sleep tracking data, is something I have yet to explore as I don’t sleep with my watch on, however I’m considering adding that to my routine since I’m so happy with the rest of the functionality in this app.

Love to see the continued updates being pushed frequently and Gentler Streaks getting better and better. Keep up the great work. 🏋🏻

title.label: Paid for Lifetime but Lifetime Wasn’t for Long

content.label: Now with the latest update, I’m no longer able to use Gentler Streak on my watch since I’m unable to update to iOS9. Therefore, my lifetime subscription is now useless and the app was removed from my watch. Moral of the story is a lifetime isn’t really a lifetime any longer. What a waste of money!

I really liked this app, even if I wasn’t consistent in using it. I’ve tried different workout tracking apps and this one was the one that really clicked with me. Unfortunately I’m going to have to delete it, as it no longer supports anything before watch OS 9. I have an older Apple Watch, a series 3, and as it doesn’t support OS 9, I have to find a new app.

title.label: Don’t use Apple health vo2 max to assess fitness.

content.label:
Gentler streak is using Apple health’s Vo2max assessment to plot an activity path, unfortunately Apple’s vo2max assessment doesn’t take into consideration the fact that when I hike I’m walking steep mountain trails, carrying a heavy pack, and so it assumes I’m far less fit than I am. 
That breaks the deal for me, either be accurate or I’m not interested.

title.label: Love the app, but it stopped working

content.label: I rely on this app to guide my exercise, but ever since a recent update, the activity streak and wellness dashboard have completely stopped loading. I have iOS 15, which I believe is still supported, and I’ve tried uninstalling and reinstalling with the same result. It’s a real bummer to be greeted with the progress wheel whenever I try to check my status!

Not the best app if you use other apps to track your workouts. I have an app that I use to log my strength training workouts which syncs with Apple Health. However, that data does not sync to gentler streak. When I try to manually add these workouts, they don’t save. I’ll most likely end up deleting the app which is unfortunate because I like the idea of it.

title.label: I like the idea but it really didn’t work for me

content.label: After watching me for 7 days it told me immediately to take a day off. So I did. I had been exercising daily so why not. Then the next day it told me again, take the day off. You need to rest. Then halfway through the day it told me I need to step up my game because I’ve taken two days off. Then today it said the same thing. I did a fairly rigorous workout and it didn’t register at all. So I think I’ll stick with just listening to my body. Great idea. Very cute. Would like more stats. Most things I’d like to know were hidden behind tabs I wouldn’t think they’d be under or not available at all. Maybe I’ll try it again down the road.
Wish I had known. Asking for a subscription refund now. No explicit guidance that a smartwatch is essential. Until you try to use it. But it absolutely is. Really should be upfront about this.

App says it needs 7 days to learn my workout habits. I gave it about ten days, opened the app to “0” records. There are troubleshooting instructions on the app, but I don’t have the time or energy to fix things like this - I expect them to work as expected. I have requested a refund.

The app is simple, can track everything I do and it tells me when to stop, I tend to workout too much. The only flaw is when you end workouts it will sometime restart the workout. This often messes with my tin times and there’s no way to fix it.
I signed up for the free 7 day trial and was immediately charged $11. I can’t find it in my apple purchases to dispute it or anything.
I did a surf, a lift and a 24 minute rollerblade over the span of 4 days and it says I’m pushing too hard and need to rest. That can’t be accurate. Moving on…
I wanted to cancel and request a refund,  I could not find the ability to cancel or the trial period in the program but I contacted Apple directly and I did receive full refund..

title.label: Not worth it if you don’t have an Apple Watch

content.label: I love the idea, but you really need an Apple Watch to make it work. In theory, it’s supposed to work as long as all your data is in the apple health app. But if you don’t have a fitness tracker, or your tracker is a Fitbit, all your data isn’t going to be in the apple health app, and then it’s not going to do much for you. (There are separate 3rd party apps that sync Fitbit with AH, but they all seem sketchy - personally I don’t like to give out my data like that.) You have to pay to be able to add things to Gentler Streaks manually, and even then it keeps displaying things about fitness trackers, like telling you to wear your smartwatch to bed. They should really make it clear up front that 99% of the functions are based on having an Apple Watch.

Out of any app that I’ve used in the past, this one gives the best Heart Rate Zone tools. I end up copying what I have in Gentler and put it in the Apple Watch workout activity settings. What I get from the Apple Watch by default doesn’t feel as accurate as Gentler.

I feel like I’m barely doing anything. 
This would be better for someone who has health issues or is just starting out.
There is nothing more on premium than on free except for a few “inspirational” videos. Don’t get tricked like I did. Don’t waste your money. This app does not provide what it promises.

This so-called app is simply an interactive advertisement pushing you to buy a subscription.  Every screen showcases features you can’t use without paying, while minimizing the features you can actually use.  Why pretend to be a free app???  It’d be much more honest to charge for the app up front.
Apples fitness app seems to be made by and for robots. This does a lovely job of sitting on top and turning it into a product for humans.

I’ve used a lot of different fitness trackers over the years but this one has one of the cleanest designs, smallest amount of bugs, and overall functionality that I’ve seen. Especially a fan of how it was able to import all of my Nike Run Club since 2015 and I can see my run totals from each year since then. (I hope soon they’ll be able to bring in the stuff from 2011-2014 too). 

Would definitely recommend.

How come my feedback always says that I’ve retained my fitness but my weekly, monthly, and yearly graphs show sharp increases in fitnesses, even far above the grey line? I feel like the daily feedback doesn’t match the longer term reality. It’s pretty disheartening, too, to do a strong workout and see it tell me I’ve just “maintained” and not increased my fitnesses. I hope that’s not really what’s happening.

title.label: Great premise, very slow to load 🫤

content.label:
I really love the concept of the app, but it is incredibly slow to open and load data (noticeably slower than other data intensive apps). If I’m trying to get a quick sense of where I’m at in the day this is often enough delay that I just close the app and move on. If I open a month in review, it has to process the data again it seems, even if I’ve looked at the month before.

I like that the app helps focus on relative effort, and encourages you to get back into things, well, gently. It’s so much nicer than apps that don’t afford any rest time or that don’t account for overall wellness when setting goals and determining steaks.

I’ll keep with it for now at least!

I expected a lot more out of a $30 app. The rest tracker is interesting and what drew me into the app, but I wouldn’t have paid $30 if I knew that was essentially all it was.

The data it tracks can already be tracked via your apple watch, fitness, and health app. The rest of the content is pretty worthless as well. It’s a bunch of regurgitated summaries of fitness articles. 

I could maybe see this being helpful if you are 100% new fitness but the app doesn’t offer much else if you’re already on your fitness journey. 

Beyond the rest tracker you’re basically paying $30/year to reskin the fitness and health app that already comes on your phone.
You can only do an eighth of the things on here without premium

title.label: An app that finally validates my daily movements.

content.label:
At my current job, I end up walking between 14k-24k steps (~7-12 miles) in a singular 5-10 hour shift. It’s exhausting both physically and mentally, and there’s obviously no point in me trying to add in an “official” walk/run exercise on any of the days that I’m working.

I was a bit hesitant to try this app out after reading a handful of reviews that talked about how they “wished the activity path would include daily steps” in it’s calculations. Obviously, the only metric I’m actually measuring while at work IS, in fact, my daily step count, alongside occasional heart rate readings and “idle” exercise minutes (~60-150min total) that get tracked outside of official workouts.

DAILY STEPS DO HAVE AN EFFECT ON THE ACTIVITY PATHWAY!

I don’t know how many daily steps those other reviewers were counting, but I can see a major difference in my activity path between the 4 days that I work 9-10 hours, the day I work 5 hours, and the 2 days I get off during the week. The difference is blatantly obviously when you move as much as I do during a work shift.

This app really makes me feel validated in my physical fitness. I can’t begin to tell you how many times I would come home from work and think to myself something along the lines of, “You shouldn’t be this tired. You’re not doing much of anything worth feeling tired over.” But this app is the first thing to tell me that I’m pushing myself hard, that I’m edging towards the limits of my physical capabilities, that I should take a day to rest and recover (which I sadly can’t because it’s my job).

The “Go Gentler” workouts are also really nice. I really like the interface on the Apple Watch and how it shows you your HR zones as the default screen during an exercise. (I know Apple’s Exercise app supposedly has a screen for HR zones too but I can’t figure out how to show that while exercising.)

I think my one recommendation/request for this app going forward would be the ability to customize the “Go Gentler” workouts, which doesn’t seem to be an option as far as I can tell. Apple’s Exercise app lets you set up custom workouts with intervals, repetitions, and has the option for warmup and cooldown times. If there was a way to do that with the “Go Gentler” workouts too, I think this app would be nearing perfection.

I’ve been using Gentler Streak for about 2 months and find it to be very useful in staying on track with my exercise plan. I like the way it tracks and provides the king of coaching I need. 
I have one recommendation though; it would be nice if it could be set to notify me with a gentle buzz when I’m outside my target heart rate zone, both high and low.

I love that you have more options for workouts like SUP or simply Kayaking. Would you please add Rucking 🙏🏻 
5 stars

I really had my doubts about this app. But I was suffering from exhaustion as I kept Apple recommendation of active life. So I gave  this app a run and by god this app has helped me so much now I am keeping me active level and not so tired all the time   I am not sure if this app is good for young people as they are supposed to challenge their bodies as they grow up but for me , a man is his 50’s , and I had my challenge  period behind me, this is a  god sent app that is helping me stay active and not destroying my body   Thank you guys and keep up the great work
There is too much over reaching. I’d rather use the fitness tracker.
